entity.name: Christopher Dodd
entity.description: Independent developer maintaining NYX, a local-first Android AI workstation focused on user control, privacy, and accessible on-device AI workflows. Seeking support to improve reliability, documentation, testing, and open-source sustainability.

projects.name: NYX
projects.description: NYX is a Kotlin and Jetpack Compose local-first Android AI workstation with implemented native GGUF CPU inference through bundled llama.cpp, local Ollama and explicitly configured OpenAI-compatible providers, streaming chat, persisted history, bounded objective execution, permission-scoped Termux/Debian development, verified Workbench artifacts, guarded URL research, and Android Keystore-backed credentials. The public release is v0.8.9; v0.9.0 Project Bedrock is an unpublished engineering candidate. Host/build regressions do not establish physical-device, real-provider, performance or operating-system isolation guarantees. Approved project scripts remain trusted executable code; NYX does not claim an unrestricted autonomous terminal sandbox. Funding would support wider Android device testing, security and recovery regressions, reliable authorized workflows, accessibility, onboarding, and reproducible open-source verification.

channels.description: Banking and tax information will be provided privately to an approved grant administrator after award verification. Do not publish bank details.

plans.name: NYX open-source Android development grant
plans.description: Six-month $10,000 development plan: $6,000 maintainer time; $1,500 Android device testing; $1,000 security and regression tests; $1,000 documentation and onboarding; $500 build and release infrastructure. Deliverables: tested Android builds, reliable local-model agents and workflows, accessibility improvements, setup guides, and reproducible open-source releases. Funding is requested, not awarded.
